nodes.label: Hero is pure CSS, not JavaScript — title, tagline, buttons and rule animate via keyframes so the most important content never depends on a script to become visible (a stalled JS animation would otherwise leave the hero blank); Hero, SplitWords, RangeRule stay server components

nodes.label: LazyMotion + m components load only the domAnimation feature set instead of the full Framer Motion build (components import m, not motion, enforced by 'strict'), cutting First Load JS from 168kB to 144kB despite adding the whole motion system
nodes.norm_label: lazymotion + m components load only the domanimation feature set instead of the full framer motion build (components import m, not motion, enforced by 'strict'), cutting first load js from 168kb to 144kb despite adding the whole motion system

nodes.label: MotionConfig reducedMotion='user' neutralizes Framer transform animations, and a CSS killswitch in globals.css neutralizes keyframes including delays — otherwise a prefers-reduced-motion visitor would stare at hidden content through the longest delay before it snaps into view
nodes.norm_label: motionconfig reducedmotion='user' neutralizes framer transform animations, and a css killswitch in globals.css neutralizes keyframes including delays — otherwise a prefers-reduced-motion visitor would stare at hidden content through the longest delay before it snaps into view

nodes.label: Motion system prioritizes care over quantity per the brief's 'sober use only' constraint — few, fully orchestrated movements, none decorative; single shared expo-out easing [0.16,1,0.3,1] and duration scale from lib/motion.ts; only transform/opacity animated, never layout, so zero reflow
nodes.norm_label: motion system prioritizes care over quantity per the brief's 'sober use only' constraint — few, fully orchestrated movements, none decorative; single shared expo-out easing [0.16,1,0.3,1] and duration scale from lib/motion.ts; only transform/opacity animated, never layout, so zero reflow

nodes.label: Per-locale OG image via next/og — Satori draws Arabic glyphs correctly but skips the bidi algorithm, so the 'ar' card manually reverses its tokens and stays on one line via the rtl() helper; drop the helper if a future Satori version fixes bidi (the site itself is unaffected since the browser handles bidi)
nodes.norm_label: per-locale og image via next/og — satori draws arabic glyphs correctly but skips the bidi algorithm, so the 'ar' card manually reverses its tokens and stays on one line via the rtl() helper; drop the helper if a future satori version fixes bidi (the site itself is unaffected since the browser handles bidi)
